# `usd-cli`

usd-cli — perceive and manipulate USD scenes over a token-efficient CLI. Run `usd-cli cheatsheet` for a one-screen tour of every verb.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--version`: Show version + active backend.
* `--json`: Structured output with schema_version.
* `-q, --quiet`: Payload only; suppress summary lines.
* `--server TEXT`: Daemon URL (default: auto-discover).
* `--session TEXT`: Named session (default: USD_CLI_SESSION, then the shared default).
* `--timeout FLOAT`: Total wall-time ceiling in seconds. When set, bounds even renders/physics (default: 30s for quick commands, 1800s for render/physics).  [default: -1.0]
* `--install-completion`: Install completion for the current shell.
* `--show-completion`: Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli cheatsheet`

One-screen tour of every verb (the token-cheap alternative to --help crawls).

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli cheatsheet [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli resolve`

Reveal the full SdfPath(s) behind ref(s), or list the whole ref table.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli resolve [OPTIONS] [REFS]...
```

**Arguments**:

* `[REFS]...`: Refs to reveal; omit to list all.

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli snapshot`

Compact text tree of the scene. The core perceive step.

Refs are deterministic by SdfPath and stable within a session, so -D diffs show only
real changes.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli snapshot [OPTIONS] [SCOPE]
```

**Arguments**:

* `[SCOPE]`: Path or @ref to scope to.

**Options**:

* `-v, --visible`
* `-t, --type TEXT`: Filter by prim type (repeatable).
* `-d, --depth INTEGER`
* `-s, --scope TEXT`
* `-m, --materials`
* `-b, --bounds`
* `-p, --properties`
* `-D, --diff`: Diff vs the previous snapshot.
* `--structural`: Attribute-level diff (e.g. @n5 -t(2,0,0) +t(5,0,0)) vs text.
* `--since TEXT`: Diff against a named checkpoint.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli render`

Multimodal render — modalities combine in a single pass.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli render [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-p, --photoreal`
* `--depth`
* `-n, --normals`
* `--seg`
* `-w, --wireframe`
* `-a, --annotate`
* `--focus TEXT`: Auto-frame this @ref.
* `--orbit INTEGER`: N viewpoints around target.
* `--elevation FLOAT`
* `--res TEXT`: WxH, e.g. 1920x1080.
* `--inline`: Also return base64 inline.
* `--mode TEXT`: fast | quality (default: quality/RT2).
* `--renderer TEXT`: auto | ovrtx | remote (both explicit choices use OVRTX).
* `--against TEXT`: Render-diff vs a prior render's beauty image.
* `--diff TEXT`: Diff type for --against: visual | geometry | both. geometry diffs segmentation footprints, catching moved glass/transparent objects.
* `--exclude TEXT`: Refs to exclude (repeatable).
* `-o, --output TEXT`
* `--max-upload-mb FLOAT`: Per-render override of render.remote_max_upload_mb (0 = unlimited) — for scenes that legitimately exceed the safe default cap.
* `--detach`: Return a job id immediately; collect with `usd-cli wait <job>` — no more poll loops on long renders.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli render-frames`

Render a USD over a frame range at its time samples, with an animated GIF.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli render-frames [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--frames TEXT`: FrameSpec: '0:30' range, '0,5,10' list, or '42'. Default: the stage's full authored animation range (clamped to it).
* `--scene TEXT`: USD to play (e.g. a physics recording.usda); default: the open stage.
* `--res TEXT`: WxH.
* `--camera TEXT`: Camera @ref/path to render through.
* `--focus TEXT`: Auto-frame this @ref.
* `--fps FLOAT`: GIF frames/sec. Default: the stage's timeCodesPerSecond, else 24.
* `--mode TEXT`: fast | quality (default: quality/RT2).
* `--renderer TEXT`
* `--no-animate`: Skip the assembled GIF; keep frames only.
* `-o, --output TEXT`
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli transform`

Translate / rotate / scale a prim. +/- = relative, bare = absolute.

Tip: use '--tx=-3' (with '=') for negative values so the shell doesn't read -3 as a flag.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli transform [OPTIONS] REF
```

**Arguments**:

* `REF`: [required]

**Options**:

* `--tx, --translate-x TEXT`
* `--ty, --translate-y TEXT`
* `--tz, --translate-z TEXT`
* `--rx, --rotate-x TEXT`
* `--ry, --rotate-y TEXT`
* `--rz, --rotate-z TEXT`
* `--sx, --scale-x TEXT`
* `--sy, --scale-y TEXT`
* `--sz, --scale-z TEXT`
* `--translate TEXT`: Vector x,y,z.
* `--rotate TEXT`: Vector x,y,z (degrees).
* `--scale TEXT`: Vector x,y,z.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli material`

Set/bind material properties — on one @ref, a named --subset, or a bulk rule
selection (--all/--type/--where/--under). Default authors a UsdPreviewSurface;
--omnipbr / --mdl author an MDL material instead; --unbind removes the binding;
'material audit' reports bound/unbound renderables, subsets, and unused materials.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli material [OPTIONS] [REF]
```

**Arguments**:

* `[REF]`: Target @ref/path; 'audit' runs the binding audit; omit for bulk selection.

**Options**:

* `--color TEXT`: r,g,b in 0..1.
* `--metallic FLOAT`
* `--roughness FLOAT`
* `--opacity FLOAT`
* `--clearcoat FLOAT`: Clearcoat weight 0..1.
* `--clearcoat-roughness FLOAT`
* `--ior FLOAT`: Index of refraction.
* `--emissive TEXT`: Emissive color r,g,b.
* `--bind TEXT`: Bind existing material @m.
* `--unbind`: Remove the prim's direct material binding.
* `--omnipbr`: Author an MDL OmniPBR material.
* `--mdl TEXT`: MDL module asset, e.g. OmniGlass.mdl (implies MDL).
* `--mdl-id TEXT`: MDL subIdentifier (defaults to the module stem).
* `--diffuse-tex TEXT`: Albedo map.
* `--normal-tex TEXT`: Normal map.
* `--orm-tex TEXT`: ORM map (MDL).
* `--roughness-tex TEXT`: Roughness map (preview surface).
* `--metallic-tex TEXT`: Metallic map (preview surface).
* `--uv-set TEXT`: UV primvar (default st).
* `--tex-scale TEXT`: Texture UV scale su,sv.
* `--tex-rotate FLOAT`: Texture UV rotation (deg).
* `--tex-translate TEXT`: Texture UV offset tu,tv.
* `--input TEXT`: Raw shader input name=value (repeatable).
* `--all`: Bulk mode: select prims by rule instead of a ref.
* `-t, --type TEXT`: Bulk filter: prim type (repeatable).
* `--where TEXT`: Bulk rule, e.g. 'name~=Conductor*' (repeatable, ANDed).
* `--under TEXT`: Bulk scope: subtree @ref/path.
* `--subset TEXT`: Bind on a named GeomSubset of the mesh (per-face).
* `--prototype`: Author on the instanced prim's prototype source (all instances pick it up).
* `--effective`: audit: list every renderable's resolved material.
* `--include-subsets`: audit: include GeomSubset coverage.
* `--library TEXT`: Reference a material from a library USD.
* `--library-prim TEXT`: Exact absolute material prim path inside --library.
* `--name TEXT`: Name for the new/library material.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli material-apply`

Apply every exact path/material tuple from a decision plan in one transaction.

The plan remains the source of truth: this command does not infer targets, expand
globs, or recalculate material choices. It accepts the material workflow decision
patch schema and returns per-group/per-path receipts in one daemon response.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli material-apply [OPTIONS] PLAN
```

**Arguments**:

* `PLAN`: JSON material decision plan containing exact path assignments.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--library TEXT`: Material library USD.  [required]
* `--path-key TEXT`: Assignment path field to apply (prim_paths/source_prim_paths/runtime_prim_paths).  [default: prim_paths]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli open`

Load a USD file.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli open [OPTIONS] FILE
```

**Arguments**:

* `FILE`: Path to .usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--read-only`: Open for parallel inspection: bypasses the one-writer-per-file guard and blocks every mutating command in this session. Readers share the writer's LIVE layer, so they see its unsaved edits as they happen; any number of readers may coexist with one writer.
* `--force-reload`: Re-open the file this session already holds even if it has unsaved edits, deliberately DISCARDING them and reloading from disk.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli save`

Save the current stage (atomic: temp sibling, verify read-back, then rename;
a symlink destination is written through to its target, preserving the link).

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli save [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

**Arguments**:

* `[PATH]`

**Options**:

* `--flatten`: Composition-flatten the stage into one layer: localizes composition arcs — sublayers, references (e.g. `material --library`), payloads — into the saved file. External texture/asset FILES remain referenced, not embedded; save to .usdz to package them.
* `--detach`: Return a job id immediately (big-scene saves recompose for minutes); collect with `usd-cli wait`.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli viewer-snapshot`

```console
$ usd-cli viewer-snapshot [OPTIONS] PATH
```

**Options**:

* `--since-revision INTEGER RANGE`: Skip publication when the live stage has not changed since this revision.  [default: -1; x>=-1]
* `--line-geometry TEXT`: Viewer-owned NPZ path for the realtime technical-line pass.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `usd-cli cancel`

Cooperatively cancel a detached camera-analysis job.

**Usage**:

## `usd-cli space`

Find empty space: where an object fits, and where it can rest.

Read-only: reports regions as a floor surface plus its bounding box, and places nothing. Every point inside a region's floor fits the size you asked about.
  usd-cli space support --size 0.3,0.3,0.3 --container @n5

Needs the 'space' extra (warp-lang)

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli space [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `free`: How much room is left, ranked by volume.
* `support`: Where one object of --size can rest...

### `usd-cli space free`

How much room is left, ranked by volume.

A container's capacity is this verb with --container and --exclude-others:

    usd-cli space free --size 0.3,0.3,0.3 --exclude-others --container @cab_l,@cab_r,@cab_back,@cab_base

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli space free [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-s, --size TEXT`: Object size 'x,y,z' in stage units (one number = a cube).  [required]
* `--container TEXT`: Measure inside this container instead of the open stage. Comma-separated, or repeat the flag. Pass one geometric container prim, or however many structural component prims it is made of — they are taken together as one thing. An assembly parent is allowed for bounds, but --exclude-others needs wall/deck components explicitly so it can remove contents safely. Bounds the search AND defines what counts as the container itself for --exclude-others. e.g. --container @l,@r,@back,@base
* `--exclude-others`: Drop every triangle that is not part of --container, so the answer is what the container itself affords rather than what fits around its current contents. This is how you ask for capacity. Requires --container.
* `--interior`: Only the space enclosed by --container, not the space above it. Off by default because an open-top container — a pallet deck, a table, a flat shelf — is loaded on its top face. Pass it for a bookshelf, where the top of the unit is reachable but nobody stacks there.
* `--scope TEXT`: Explicit world AABB 'minx,miny,minz,maxx,maxy,maxz'. Intersected with --container when both are given.
* `--cell FLOAT`: Grid resolution in stage units (default: a quarter of the object's footprint).
* `--stack-height FLOAT`: Cap each region's height, in stage units. Default: the real clearance up to whatever is overhead — 'how much is left'. Pass the object's height for a one-layer placement slab instead.
* `--tau FLOAT`: Support fraction required, 0-1. 1.0 = the whole footprint rests on surface; lower allows overhang, provided the centre of gravity stays supported and the part hanging off is clear of geometry over the object's height.  [default: 1.0]
* `--margin FLOAT`: Delete support narrower than twice this, in stage units — a rim, a corner, a strip an object could only perch on. NOT an inset: a broad surface keeps its full extent, edge included. Pad --size for a stand-off from the drop.  [default: 0.0]
* `--smooth / --no-smooth`: Bridge slat/grating gaps across the object's footprint (default on). --no-smooth reports a pallet deck as unusable, which is what the raw spans say; useful for seeing what the bridging buys.  [default: smooth]
* `--merge-gap FLOAT`: Coincidence tolerance for the solid-layer merge, in stage units. Two surfaces in one column with less air than this between them are read as touching. The default (1 mm) is invisible unless --size is shorter than it, because a merged gap is too thin for anything taller to have used; below that, lower it or real resting surfaces are fused away.
* `--device TEXT`: auto | cpu | cuda. auto (default) picks cuda whenever Warp reports a usable CUDA device — measured 4.7x on a 2.3M-triangle scene, and never slower at any size tested. Pass cpu explicitly when a result must be reproducible across machines: the two devices are each deterministic but can differ slightly on geometry dense enough to overflow the per-cell solid-layer buffer. The resolved device is echoed in the summary.  [default: auto]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `usd-cli space support`

Where one object of --size can rest stably, ranked by support area.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli space support [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-s, --size TEXT`: Object size 'x,y,z' in stage units (one number = a cube).  [required]
* `--container TEXT`: Measure inside this container instead of the open stage. Comma-separated, or repeat the flag. Pass one geometric container prim, or however many structural component prims it is made of — they are taken together as one thing. An assembly parent is allowed for bounds, but --exclude-others needs wall/deck components explicitly so it can remove contents safely. * `--exclude-others`: Drop every triangle that is not part of --container, so the answer is what the container itself affords rather than what fits around its current contents. This is how you ask for capacity. Requires --container.
* `--interior`: Only the space enclosed by --container, not the space above it. Off by default because an open-top container — a pallet deck, a table, a flat shelf — is loaded on its top face. Pass it for a bookshelf, where the top of the unit is reachable but nobody stacks there.
* `--scope TEXT`: Explicit world AABB 'minx,miny,minz,maxx,maxy,maxz'. Intersected with --container when both are given.
* `--cell FLOAT`: Grid resolution in stage units (default: a quarter of the object's footprint).
* `--tau FLOAT`: Support fraction required, 0-1. 1.0 = the whole footprint rests on surface; lower allows overhang, provided the centre of gravity stays supported and the part hanging off is clear of geometry over the object's height.  [default: 1.0]
* `--margin FLOAT`: Delete support narrower than twice this, in stage units — a rim, a corner, a strip an object could only perch on. NOT an inset: a broad surface keeps its full extent, edge included. Pad --size for a stand-off from the drop.  [default: 0.0]
* `--smooth / --no-smooth`: Bridge slat/grating gaps across the object's footprint (default on). --no-smooth reports a pallet deck as unusable, which is what the raw spans say; useful for seeing what the bridging buys.  [default: smooth]
* `--merge-gap FLOAT`: Coincidence tolerance for the solid-layer merge, in stage units. Two surfaces in one column with less air than this between them are read as touching. The default (1 mm) is invisible unless --size is shorter than it, because a merged gap is too thin for anything taller to have used; below that, lower it or real resting surfaces are fused away.
* `--device TEXT`: auto | cpu | cuda. auto (default) picks cuda whenever Warp reports a usable CUDA device — measured 4.7x on a 2.3M-triangle scene, and never slower at any size tested. Pass cpu explicitly when a result must be reproducible across machines: the two devices are each deterministic but can differ slightly on geometry dense enough to overflow the per-cell solid-layer buffer. The resolved device is echoed in the summary.  [default: auto]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

```console
$ usd-cli camera coverage [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--scope TEXT`: Floor/region @ref or path.
* `--camera TEXT`: Camera or rig-subtree @ref/path; repeat for multiple selections.
* `--cameras TEXT`: Comma-separated camera @refs/paths.
* `--target FLOAT`: Required coverage fraction.  [default: 0.95]
* `--per-cell INTEGER`: Required views per sampled cell.  [default: 1]
* `--grid INTEGER`: Cells along the longer scope axis.  [default: 32]
* `--cell-size FLOAT`: Grid cell size in canonical metres.
* `--device TEXT`: Warp device, e.g. cpu or cuda:0.  [default: cpu]
* `-o, --output TEXT`: Write full JSON report.
* `--detach`: Return a job id; collect with `usd-cli wait` or stop with `usd-cli cancel JOB`.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `usd-cli camera place`

Preview or author a coverage-aware multi-camera rig.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli camera place [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--method TEXT`: max_coverage or look_at.  [required]
* `--scope TEXT`: Region for max_coverage.
* `--target TEXT`: Object for look_at.
* `--target-coverage FLOAT`: Coverage target (default: 0.95).
* `--per-cell INTEGER`: Views required per grid cell (default: 1).
* `--max-cameras INTEGER`: Coverage camera limit (default: 8).
* `--cameras INTEGER`: Exact look_at camera count (default: 4).
* `--grid INTEGER`: Coverage grid long-axis cells (default: 32).
* `--patch-size, --cell-size FLOAT`: Coverage patch size in canonical metres; mutually exclusive with --grid.
* `--candidates INTEGER`: [default: 64]
* `--height FLOAT`: Metres above floor (max_coverage default: 3) or target-center offset (look_at default: 0).
* `--min-height FLOAT`: Minimum look_at height above the target center in canonical metres.
* `--max-height FLOAT`: Maximum look_at height above the target center in canonical metres.
* `--standoff FLOAT`: Coverage perimeter standoff in metres (default: 0.5).
* `--minimum-gain FLOAT`: Minimum coverage marginal gain (default: 0).
* `--min-look-down FLOAT`: Minimum pitch below horizontal in degrees.
* `--max-look-down FLOAT`: Maximum pitch below horizontal in degrees.
* `--yaw-ranges TEXT`: Allowed look_at bearings, e.g. '0,180;270,360'.
* `--occlusion-threshold FLOAT`: Maximum look_at occlusion (default: 0.4).
* `--min-distance FLOAT`
* `--max-distance FLOAT`
* `--min-x FLOAT`: Minimum look_at camera X in canonical metres.
* `--max-x FLOAT`: Maximum look_at camera X in canonical metres.
* `--min-y FLOAT`: Minimum look_at camera Y in canonical metres.
* `--max-y FLOAT`: Maximum look_at camera Y in canonical metres.
* `--allow-fewer`
* `--seed INTEGER`: [default: 0]
* `--focal FLOAT`
* `--aperture FLOAT`: [default: 36.0]
* `--device TEXT`: [default: cpu]
* `--preview`: Explicitly request no stage mutation.
* `--author-under TEXT`: Atomically author the accepted rig below this path.
* `--on-existing TEXT`: error, replace, or append.  [default: error]
* `-o, --output TEXT`: Write full JSON report.
* `--detach`: Return a job id; collect with `usd-cli wait` or stop with `usd-cli cancel JOB`.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `usd-cli camera rig-export`

Export canonical intrinsics, extrinsics, visibility, and verification evidence.

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Set renderer=remote + remote_url in config, then probe the service's /health.

Read a bearer key from OVRTX_API_KEY (or USD_CLI_RENDER_REMOTE_API_KEY), never
from a command-line argument.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli remote configure [OPTIONS] URL
```

**Arguments**:

* `URL`: Remote service URL, e.g. http://gpu-host:8000.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--add`: Append to the configured backend pool instead of replacing the primary (parallel rendering).
* `--global`: Write to ~/.config/usd-cli (default: project).
* `--no-test`: Skip the /health probe.
* `--timeout FLOAT`: Health-probe timeout (seconds).  [default: 10.0]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

```console
$ usd-cli remote backends [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--timeout FLOAT`: Per-backend probe timeout (seconds).  [default: 5.0]
* `--deep`: Also run a tiny REAL render per backend (a cube, 64x64) — proves GPU render capability, not just HTTP reachability. Round 7: /live stayed green while every render 500'd (the containers had lost GPU access).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

* `-f, --file TEXT`: JSON operations patch (or '-' for stdin).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `usd-cli physics validate`

Deterministic schema validation (mass/density finite, no nested rigid bodies, etc.).

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli physics validate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `usd-cli physics simulate`

Simulate an explicit scenario → time-sampled recording.usda + raw metrics.

Play the result with `render-frames --scene <recording.usda>`.

**Usage**:

```console
$ usd-cli physics simulate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--scene TEXT`: Pre-authored simulation USD.  [required]
* `--body TEXT`: Exact simulated body @ref/path used to author the recording.  [required]
* `--body-pattern TEXT`: Optional ovphysx solver binding pattern; defaults to --body.
* `--rest-position TEXT`: Metric rest position as X,Y,Z.  [required]
* `--world-up TEXT`: Metric up direction as X,Y,Z.  [required]
* `--engine TEXT`: ovphysx (real solver; local on supported Linux or Windows hosts, otherwise through the managed OVRTX adapter when it advertises physics support).  [default: ovphysx]
* `--duration FLOAT`: Sim duration (s).  [default: 1.0]
* `--fps INTEGER`: Trajectory sample rate.  [default: 30]
* `--dt FLOAT`: Solver timestep (s).  [default: 0.004166666666666667]
* `-o, --output TEXT`
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.
